agency.name: Workers' Compensation Division, Department of Consumer and Business Services (WCD)

ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: 66-2/3 percent of wages, but not more than 133 percent of the state average weekly wage (ORS 656.210(1)). For workers with more than one job, wages from all subject employment are added (ORS 656.210(2)).
ttd.minText: Not less than 90 percent of wages a week or $50 a week, whichever is less (ORS 656.210(1)).
ttd.periodLabel: injuries from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (SAWW $1,461.21; maximum = 133% of SAWW)

waiting.text: No temporary disability is payable for the first three calendar days after the worker leaves work, unless total disability continues for 14 consecutive days or the worker is admitted as a hospital inpatient within 14 days of the first onset of total disability (ORS 656.210(3)).

ttdDuration.text: ORS 656.210 sets no week limit; temporary total disability is paid during the period of total disability.

ppd.text: Impairment benefits = impairment value x 100 x the state average weekly wage (ORS 656.214(2)(a)). If the worker is not released or returned to regular work, a work-disability award is added: impairment modified by age, education and adaptability x 150 x the worker's weekly wage, the wage factor being limited to 50%-133% of the SAWW (ORS 656.214(2)(b)). Awards over $6,000 are paid at 4.35 times the weekly TTD rate (Bulletin 111, ORS 656.216).

facts.text: Workers who are not otherwise eligible for an increase have their temporary total disability benefits raised each fiscal year by the percentage increase of the state average weekly wage (ORS 656.210(1)); the SAWW rose 3.116% to $1,461.21 on July 1, 2026.
A worker with more than one job can receive supplemental disability for wages lost from the additional jobs if the insurer is notified within 30 days of the claim (ORS 656.210(2)).

The first disability payment must be issued by the 14th day after the employer knows of the claim and of the disability, and lost wages are paid until a decision if the insurer takes longer than 14 days to decide.
Workers also receive temporary disability when they must leave work to receive medical services for an accepted disabling injury (ORS 656.210(4)).
